failureWasRecorded.description: first judgement: whether the worker's transcript shows the new test failing through the harness on the base's code before the edit was built, and then passing (check 3); second judgement: whether each assertion that closes a finding of your refusal was shown failing at the refused head by your own program and passes in the repair round's recorded run; false for a rung that edits only prose, which has none

loudToQuiet.description: whether a loud failure became a quiet value, and what the value is

stopsMet.description: every stop the batch record's intro reserves for Pavol that was met, including one met on part of the work while the rest lands; empty if none

rung.description: the rung id; the review names it, a rung worker or skeptic may leave it empty

stop.description: the stop, in the intro's words

liftedBy.description: the POSITIONS.md line of the decision of Pavol's that lifts it; empty if none does, and then it holds the push

skepticText.description: the single word committed once SKEPTIC.md is committed on the rung's branch, where the gather reads it; the full text of this judgement, word for word, only when the harness refused your write, for the gather to write verbatim

forPavol.description: every point for Pavol this skeptic finds that the rung does not settle, one entry each with its evidence as file:line; the gather puts each into PLAN.md; empty if none

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

POSITIONS.md:25
- **The specification stays the standard, the Types chapter beside it.** Where the Types chapter of the team's unfinished restart (`Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick`) covers a topic, it is cited beside `Specification/` as the designers' later word: the exclusion rule as "instantiation exclusion" in its two-part form, the `covariant` modifier, `Bottom` inexpressible. "On the rule S revises, it is the designers' latest intent, and the goal is to finish what they intended."

POSITIONS.md:93
- **The suite's verdict is the check.** A test passes or fails, as the team designed the suite, and a value that matters is asserted in the test with the mechanisms the suite already has (an `assert` in an interpreter test, `run_out_equals` in a compiled one): "what is the purpose of a test suit that you just cannot run it and get a green? If everything that's encoded in it is, is okay and it turns red if it's not, why would you have to compare some values that it outputs? Those values must be part of the test." What a test prints beyond its checks does not matter: "When the designers of the test suite decided that it passes without any additional check, it is not needed to control its outputs." So no batch compares the corpus's printed outputs, no baseline is run to compare against, and no expected-output files are added to the interpreter suite, which has none; none of it is offered to him again.

POSITIONS.md:44
- **The static-parameter sentence goes (answer 9).** The specification's sentence that overloads may not differ in static parameters is dropped; the specification is revised to the type group's 2011 model the checker runs, the original kept as superseded text in the S1 form. The checker keeps the paper's three rules with two changes: the return-type rule is checked over every instance, and one narrow rule stays, that two generic arms in the more-specific relation agree on their static parameters position by position (Java's overriding rule; it closes row 398). Walk dispatches by declared domains, which ends its dependence on declaration order. The library's refused families are repaired by its own devices. No model line changes. Built: the specification states the 2011 model; the checker checks the return-type rule over every instance, and the positional rule, return-type condition only, for two declarations with as many static parameters of their own, the scope listed for his review; walk chooses by declared domains; the library's families are repaired by its own exclusions but for `seq`'s remaining pairs (FACTS, "The specification states the type group's 2011 overloading model ...", "The compiled checker checks the Return Type Rule over every instance and answer 9's positional rule", "Walk chooses between a generic declaration and another on their declared domains ..." and "The one library's refused overload families are repaired by its own exclusions ..."). The judgement's section 10 items (walk and an unused unknown size, `seq`'s device, Naden's instantiation) took the record's defaults, listed for his review, and what the build left open for him is listed in `PLAN.md` beside them.

POSITIONS.md:43
- **`AnyIntegral`'s closure and how the checker reads `comprises`.** The generic scalar-extension block with its two unnamed choices, the `AnyAdditiveGroup` marker and the `Array3` exclusion stand as landed, and so does the closure `AnyIntegral comprises { ... }`, with a `NOT YET`-style comment in the team's wording at the line. Built. Of the api's overloading and return-type errors this let through, answer 9's families are repaired by the library's own exclusions, `seq`'s remaining pairs aside (FACTS, "The one library's refused overload families are repaired by its own exclusions ..."), and the meet rule and the residue are batch 8's.

POSITIONS.md:50
- **The `comprises` passages read at the level of values (PLAN item 26, row 491).** The four passages of the specification that read a `comprises` clause at the level of types are restated at the level of values, "covers" is defined once, the Meet Rule has the closed-trait case, and row 492 is repaired on both paths; the proof appendix keeps its existence lemmas and gives up static uniqueness for run-time uniqueness, a call whose argument's static type sits between typed by the intersection of its candidates' return types. Built (FACTS, "The specification gives the run-time instance of a dispatched declaration ...", "The compiled checker accepts the Meet Rule's `comprises` example by a coverage check local to overload checking ..." and "Walk's load check reads a generic declaration beside a plain one on declared domains ..."). The separate analysis session's proof addendum (`reviews/comprises-type-level-proof-addendum.md`, written at his request: he was "super scared that we are touching type theoretical things that I am totally unequipped to handle") has three points built in: Fortress already dispatches at run time with one static winner, so the performance cost claimed for such calls is unproven; the coverage search stays local to overload checking and does not widen assignment or ordinary subtyping; the proof holds only where closed families are closed, which row 487 leaves unenforced across some component boundaries. The boundary (Astra's): the proof justifies the return-type intersection for ground declarations only, the more specific declarations that may run included; a generic declaration that needs a run-time instantiation must meet every static return promise at once, so the typing rule is not generalized on the proof; a generic argument already instantiated, such as `G[ZZ32]`, stays in the ground case. == Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:531-651

\section{Declarations with Static Parameters}
\seclabel{overloading-static-params}

The rules above compare the parameter types and the return types of
declarations without static parameters.
A declaration with static parameters is read as one declaration whose parameter
type ranges over every instance of it whose static arguments satisfy their
bounds (\secref{overloading-terms}).
A declaration $d_1$ is more specific than a declaration $d_2$ when $d_2$ is
applicable to every call to which $d_1$ is applicable, and not the other way
round (\secref{resolving-overloading}); where neither has static parameters,
this is the relation $\Ps \strictsubtype \Qs$ of the rules above.
A set of overloaded declarations, some or all of which have static parameters,
is a valid overloading when every pair $d_1$, $d_2$ of them satisfies the
following three rules:
\begin{itemize}
\item
The \emph{No Duplicates Rule}: $d_1$ and $d_2$ are not each more specific than
the other.
\item
The \emph{Meet Rule}: $d_1$ and $d_2$ exclude each other, or one of them is more
specific than the other, or some declaration of the set is more specific than
both and applicable to every call to which both are applicable.
\item
The \emph{Return Type Rule}: if $d_1$ is more specific than $d_2$, then for
every argument type other than \TYP{BottomType} to which $d_1$ is applicable,
and for every instance of $d_2$ that is applicable to it, some instance of $d_1$
is applicable to it whose return type is a subtype of the return type of that
instance of $d_2$.
\end{itemize}
The Subtype Rule, the Incompatibility Rule and the Meet Rule above are these
rules for declarations without static parameters, with the conditions that
coercion adds; the Return Type Rule is the Subtype Rule's condition on return
types, checked over every instance of the less specific declaration and not
over one instance chosen for the pair.

As in \secref{more-specific-rule}, declarations of the set that are each more
specific than both $d_1$ and $d_2$ and that together cover every argument to
which both are applicable also satisfy the Meet Rule.
\revision{revival-meet}{The type group's paper of 2011 states the Meet Rule
without this case.}

Two parameter types with static parameters exclude each other, for the Meet
Rule and the Incompatibility Rule, as the type group's paper of 2011 decides it
by \emph{existential reduction}: each static parameter stands for any type
within its bound, and where the two parameter types mention one parameterized
trait, instantiation exclusion (\secref{trait-types}) lets them meet only where
the static arguments of those mentions are the same, every static argument but
an operator argument counting.
So where \TYP{Box} and \TYP{Pair} are distinct object types with static
parameters, the parameter types \EXP{\TYP{Box}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket} and
\EXP{\TYP{Pair}\llbracket{}A, B\rrbracket} of two declarations exclude each
other whatever \VAR{T}, \VAR{A} and \VAR{B} stand for.

The Return Type Rule refuses the following pair, where trait \TYP{Round}
extends trait \TYP{Shape} and object \TYP{Circle} extends \TYP{Round}:
%(* Not allowed! *)
%ident[\T extends Shape\](x: T): T = x
%ident(x: Round): Round = x
\begin{Fortress}
\(\mathtt{(*}\;\hbox{\rm  Not allowed! \unskip}\;\mathtt{*)}\)\\
\(\VAR{ident}\llbracket{}T \KWD{extends} \TYP{Shape}\rrbracket(x\COLON{}T)\COLON{}T = x\)\\
\(\VAR{ident}(x\COLON \TYP{Round})\COLON \TYP{Round} = x\)
\end{Fortress}
The second declaration is more specific than the first.
For an argument of type \TYP{Circle}, the instance of the first at \TYP{Circle}
is applicable and returns a \TYP{Circle}, but the second, which runs for such an
argument, returns only a \TYP{Round}, and it has no other instance.
The pair is allowed when the second declaration is itself generic:
%ident[\T extends Shape\](x: T): T = x
%ident[\T extends Round\](x: T): T = x
\begin{Fortress}
\(\VAR{ident}\llbracket{}T \KWD{extends} \TYP{Shape}\rrbracket(x\COLON{}T)\COLON{}T = x\)\\
\(\VAR{ident}\llbracket{}T \KWD{extends} \TYP{Round}\rrbracket(x\COLON{}T)\COLON{}T = x\)
\end{Fortress}
Its instance at any type to which it is applicable returns that type.
\revision{revival-overloading}{This section is new.
The Working Draft of February 2011 required overloaded declarations to have
identical static parameters and ignored them.
The rules stated are those of the type group's paper of 2011 (Allen, Hilburn,
Kilpatrick, Luchangco, Ryu, Chase, and Steele, ``Type Checking Modular Multiple
Dispatch with Parametric Polymorphism and Multiple Inheritance'', OOPSLA 2011),
which the compiled type checker applies, with its Return Type Rule checked over
every instance of the less specific declaration; the pair refused above has the
shape of that paper's own example, which the compiled path used to accept and
then fail to verify.
Neither implementation runs the pair allowed above today: the interpreter
refuses it at load, since it asks two declarations with static
parameters for a pair of parameter types that exclude each other (row~159 of the
revival's gap ledger), and the compiled code generator fails on it (row~537).
The compiled implementation adds one restriction that is not a rule of the
language.
When one declaration with static parameters is more specific than another that
declares as many static parameters of its own, the two must declare them of the
same kinds, position by position, and the return type of the more specific one
must be a subtype of the other's when their static parameters are identified
position by position; for its code generator hands the static arguments that a call writes,
by position, to whichever declaration the call dispatches to (row~398 of the
revival's gap ledger).
So it refuses this override, whose return type names its static parameters in
the other order, where \TYP{Pr} is an object with two type parameters:
%trait Maker
%  make[\A, B\](): Pr[\A, B\]
%end
%object M extends Maker
%  make[\A, B\](): Pr[\B, A\] = Pr[\B, A\](1)
%end
\begin{Fortress}
\(\KWD{trait} \TYP{Maker}\)\\
{\tt~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(  \VAR{make}\llbracket{}A, B\rrbracket()\COLON \TYP{Pr}\llbracket{}A, B\rrbracket\)\-\\\poptabs
\(\KWD{end}\)\\
\(\KWD{object} M \KWD{extends} \TYP{Maker}\)\\
{\tt~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(  \VAR{make}\llbracket{}A, B\rrbracket()\COLON \TYP{Pr}\llbracket{}B, A\rrbracket = \TYP{Pr}\llbracket{}B, A\rrbracket(1)\)\-\\\poptabs
\(\KWD{end}\)
\end{Fortress}
The type group's paper of 2019 (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu, POPL 2019)
instantiates a dispatched declaration from the dynamic types of the arguments
and the static type of the call, renaming static parameters freely
(\secref{resolving-overloading}); under it the override is valid, and the
restriction goes when the compiled dispatcher instantiates a declaration that
way.}

736      static private boolean genericOverlapCovered(Overload gen, Overload plain, Collection<Overload> all) {
737          GenericFunctionOrMethod g = (GenericFunctionOrMethod) gen.getFn();
738          List<StaticParam> sps = g.getStaticParams();
739          Set<String> names = new HashSet<String>();
740          for (StaticParam sp : sps) names.add(NodeUtil.getName(sp));
741          List<Type> types = new ArrayList<Type>();
742          for (Param prm : g.getParams()) {
743              if (NodeUtil.isVarargsParam(prm)) return false;
744              Option<TypeOrPattern> ot = prm.getIdType();
745              if (ot.isNone()) return false;
746              types.add(NodeUtil.optTypeOrPatternToType(ot).unwrap());
747          }
748          List<FType> plainDomain = plain.getParams();
749          int n = plainDomain.size();
750          if (types.size() == 1 && n != 1 && types.get(0) instanceof TupleType) {
751              TupleType tt = (TupleType) types.get(0);
752              if (tt.getVarargs().isSome() || !tt.getKeywords().isEmpty()) return false;
753              types = tt.getElements();
754          }
755          if (types.size() != n) return false;
756          EvalType et = new EvalType(g.getWithin());
757          List<List<FType>> genDomain = new ArrayList<List<FType>>(n);
758          for (Type ty : types) {
759              List<FType> holds = new ArrayList<FType>();
760              StaticParam tp = null;
761              if (ty instanceof VarType) {
762                  String v = NodeUtil.nameString(((VarType) ty).getName());
763                  for (StaticParam sp : sps) {
764                      if (NodeUtil.isTypeParam(sp) && NodeUtil.getName(sp).equals(v)) tp = sp;
765                  }
766              }
767              if (tp != null) {
768                  for (BaseType b : tp.getExtendsClause()) {
769                      if (staticParamsNamed(b, names).isEmpty()) holds.add(et.evalType(b));
770                  }
771              } else if (staticParamsNamed(ty, names).isEmpty()) {
772                  holds.add(et.evalType(ty));
773              }
774              if (holds.isEmpty()) holds.add(FTypeTop.ONLY);
775              genDomain.add(holds);
776          }
777          return overlapCoveredBy(gen, genDomain, plain, plainDomain, all);
778      }

end

export Executable

(* A program loads when every type that extends a trait with a comprises clause is a subtype of a listed type, or a trait whose own clause lists only such types, or a trait with static parameters every extender of which is below a listed type. *)

trait AnyI comprises { A, B } end

trait A extends I[\A\] end
trait B extends I[\B\] end
object Ao extends A end
object Bo extends B end

trait S comprises { U, V } end
trait U extends S end
trait V extends S end
trait M extends S comprises { Mv } end
trait Mv extends { M, V } end
object Mo extends Mv end
object Low extends U end

trait Opt[\T\] comprises { None[\T\], Some[\T\] } end
object None[\T\] extends Opt[\T\] end
object Some[\T\](x: T) extends Opt[\T\] end

kind(x: AnyI): String = typecase x of A => "A"; else => "B" end
side(x: S): String = typecase x of U => "U"; else => "V" end
present[\T\](x: Opt[\T\]): Boolean = typecase x of Some[\T\] => true; else => false end

run(): () = do
    assert(kind(Bo), "B", "Integral's shape: the trait with static parameters I stands unlisted between AnyI and its listed types A and B, and every type that extends it is listed; Specification/basic/traits.tex, section \"Trait Declarations\"")

    assert(side(Low), "U", "an object below the listed type U")
    assert(present(Some[\ZZ32\](3)), true, "a generic object listed at its own static parameters")
    assert(present(None[\ZZ32\]), false, "the other listed generic object")
    println("PASS")
  end

end
EOF

content.description: Take the recovered 30,751-char fortress-repair-batch script (scratchpad/recovered-repair-batch.js) and write the four stages below the scatter into it, so the run no longer depends on a same-session resumeFromRunId. Keep it in the repo beside ladder-workflow.js.

content.description: Create the two wip/ worktrees from main's HEAD per remote-container.md § Setting up a batch's worktrees, push the empty branches, launch Workflow({scriptPath: explorations/coordinator/repair-batch-workflow.js, args: {base}}) on Pavol's explicit go, schedule send_later check-ins every 30 min so the Stop hook snapshots the agents' transcripts, and afterwards write the batch's report to Pavol from the returned forPavol fields.

content.subject: Land batch 6
content.description: Run wf_b262c534-337 (gate + merged-diff review, then commit). On completion: read compile-ladder/climb-batch-6/RECORD.md top; push if the commit stage held on a reversible stop (Pavol 2026-09-27: reversible stops don't block); tell Pavol the landing with F's respelled test lines as a turn's final text; no push notification at night unless stuck.

content.subject: Put the waiting branches onto main
content.description: After batch 6 lands, cherry-pick and push, then remove each worktree and branch: POSITIONS audit 2b1e4ea16 (fortress-audit); script-retry's commits in order (fortress-retry: e4fa59fde d292038ff b9c16315a 21dcccfe2, the briefing commit(s), and the proposal commit only on Pavol's go); map refresh 3ef930a34 (fortress-map); phase 3 record 7090f9595 (fortress-plan7); protocol audit bd497139f (fortress-protocol-audit) plus a P5 clause that principle 2's clean worker is the exception; the reviews fb701ff2e, d21e0bbbb, 695efd23f and the analyses 9944770ad, e71a4d1ff, each with its INDEX line. worker-context-cost.md's reading is corrected in place before it lands: low overlap between what agents searched and what the record holds shows they worked with a searchlight in a dark room, the problem itself, and is no argument against briefing; the briefing's purpose is in-context learning (Pavol 2026-09-27). Then repoint the stale protocol section references batch workers read (climb-batch-workflow.js ~127, 330, 546, 620, 896; the manual 23, 35, 51; the last POSITIONS entry). INDEX lines for reviews/mie-probes/price-keep-the-rule.md, perf-probes/prelude/exclusion-trace.md, reviews/mie-probes/scope-call-site-dispatch.md. Note in CLIMB-BATCH-6.md section 7 that the manifest gained a briefing field.

content.subject: Record Pavol's words of the night and rewrite the boot note
content.description: POSITIONS: reversible stops reserved for him don't hold a push or the next batch, listed for his review; phase 3's launch approved, Q1-Q3 defaults (a) listed for review; FACTS consolidated before each batch launches; a size's range follows the spec (nat = NN32, int = ZZ32), "Fuck yes, that's not even a question"; under How he wants to be spoken to: costs in tokens, never dollars ("I'm on a max plan. Talk to me in tokens."). Protocol hard rule 1 to match. README line to match. PLAN.md answers list, before batch 7b: (i) the where-clause sentence rung S wrote, NOT decided, plain explainer first, 7b's spec rung leaves it alone; (ii) arithmetic in a size (FortressLibrary.fss:2519, :2667, :2890; 11 errors in W1), needs his decision; (iii) rung C's two points, default take as landed, sent with 7b's walk rung. Boot note rewritten whole with the task order.

content.description: Landed at 7278e11f7 (source d65892d34), gate green against batch 6: compiler track 768 to 775, testSystem 413 to 415, checker 62 unchanged; rows 446-448; correction N made; row 418's test restated to NN32. Next comparand: climb-batch-6/followup-R/gate/.

content.description: f0958b4db: corrections folded, stale lines fixed, 47 entries verbatim to history; merged with R's lines; every briefing list passes --check; FACTS 170 KB, not shorter. Retitling pass for seven titles is a candidate.

content.subject: Launch batch 6b (rung O)
content.description: Before launch: run `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh --check` on O's list and `--common` (after the FACTS consolidation and map refresh, titles and headings must still match). In climb-batch-workflow.js: FOLLOWUP = true, LEDGER_FROM = highest ledger row + 1, O tail's POSITIONS.md:<line> citations to name base e5414f5bf; commit, push; cut /home/user/fortress-overflow on wip/rung-overflow-natives (copy ProjectFortress/build, mkdir tmp, push); Workflow({scriptPath, args:{base}}); arm a new 45-minute send_later check-in series; delete batch 6's unfired check-ins.

content.description: Conformance reviews: batch 5 (fb701ff2e, fortress-review5), batch 3 (d21e0bbbb, fortress-review3), batches 3.5/4 (695efd23f, fortress-review4) done; take all three onto main with INDEX lines. Batch 6 (F, T, R) starts once batch 6 and R land. Findings folded into tasks 24, 13, 15, 26. Pending question to Pavol: may a Fable judge rule overnight on flagged findings?

content.description: From CLIMB-BATCH-7.md: P1 (C's two rules and L, H, A devices as a shadow on the landed flat library: counts, refusals) and P4 (logging shadow of walk's generic-vs-plain choice over tests, demos, microGPT checks). One Opus worker each, shadow copies only.

content.description: After 6b lands and is pushed, and after the conformance reviews of batches 5 and 6 are read: any repair the reviews call for goes in first, as its own batch or follow-up, before phase 3. Then: small FACTS consolidation; answer 11's full switch-over distance measurement (one Opus worker); finish CLIMB-BATCH-7 counts (LEDGER_FROM, H_RIDES, P1_COUNT, comparands), splice manifest, launch batch 7 (H, A); then batch 7b (S, C, W, L) after P1/P4 with Q1-Q3 defaults (a), listed for Pavol.

content.subject: Read archaeology on knowledge-base use and act on it
content.description: Archaeology returned: no script ever required workers to read FACTS/INDEX first (ladder script of 09-17 said 'as needed'; repair and batch scripts since 09-18 offer the map as optional and cite FACTS by title in briefs); map use fell from ~80% of agents (repair batch) to ~30-35% (batches 5-6), INDEX to 0 in batch 4; no workers ever Read FACTS, only grep; no post-batch-4 review proposed enforcement; the 09-27 protocol rewrite deleted the 08-22 Scout rule unmoved (restored under task 13). Remaining: sweep for other lessons that live only in the coordinator's record and move them into the script's steps.

content.subject: Watch the running batch at 45-minute check-ins
content.description: Disk under 5 GB free is an issue (8.7 GB at 06:10 UTC); batch 6's check-in series ends 08:37 UTC; a healthy check-in ends with '.'.

content.subject: Measure map use after each batch
content.description: Pavol, 2026-09-27: get back to at least the ~80% of agents using the map that the repair batch reached after the 09-17 review. From 6b on, at each landing count per agent whether it ran step 1 (the facts-extract tool), opened the map, and used INDEX (tool_use inputs in subagents/workflows/<run>/agent-*.jsonl), and put the share in the landing report to Pavol. Write the count into the workflow manual's landing steps so it is not only in the coordinator's head.

content.description: Done and reviewed: bd497139f on protocol-audit (fortress-protocol-audit), not pushed; ten lost rules and two loose ones restored as clauses in the protocol, README and repo-internals. Taken onto main under task 12, with one clause added at P5: the clean worker of principle 2 is the one exception to pointing a brief at earlier research.

content.subject: Plan the repair batch from the batch 5 and 6 reviews
content.description: Repair batch before phase 3 (Pavol 2026-09-27), its launch his go. From batch 5's review (fb701ff2e): row 419's written fix; row 420 located then fixed; row 417 a loader lock gated by a 417-shaped program in the four-thread stage; the size range per the spec (checker refuses a size numeral outside NN32/ZZ32, a size value typed NN32/ZZ32, NatRtBigSize's expectations, row 418 restated). %makeSet[\T extends Any\](x: T): Set[\T\]

\section{Subtype Rule}
\seclabel{subtype-rule}

If the parameter type of one declaration is a subtype of the parameter
type of another (and they are not the same) then there is no
ambiguity between these two declarations: for every call to which both
are applicable, the first is more specific.  This is the basis of the
Subtype Rule.

The Subtype Rule also requires a relationship between the return types
of the two declarations.  Without such a requirement, a program may
violate type safety.

\paragraph{The Subtype Rule for Functions and Functional Methods:}
Suppose that $\f(\Ps) : \Us$ and $\f(\Qs) : \Vs$ are two distinct
function or functional method declarations in a single scope.
If $\Ps \strictsubtype \Qs$ and $\Us \Ovrsubtype \Vs$ then $\f(\Ps)$ and
$\f(\Qs)$ are a valid overloading.

Suppose that $\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$ are two functional method

\begin{itemize}

$i = j$

there is a declaration $\f(\Ps \inter \Qs)$ provide by $C$
having self parameter at $i$.

#!/bin/bash
# harness-one.sh <scratch-dir> <file.fss>... : rung C's harness-one.sh (explorations/compile-ladder/
# rung-interp-coercion/, itself rung I's shape): the testSystem harness (SystemJUTest, the class build.xml's
# testSystem shards run) over a directory holding only the named test files, with the JVM settings of
# build.xml's systemShard macro and a private cache. Run from FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh.
set -u
S=${1:?scratch dir} ; shift
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:?}
rm -rf "$S" ; mkdir -p "$S/tests" "$S/caches" "$S/tmp"
printf '\0\0\0\0' > "$S/caches/global.map"
for f in "$@" ; do cp "$f" "$S/tests/" ; done
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
echo "# harness-one $(date -u +%FT%TZ); tree $(git -C "$FH" rev-parse --short HEAD); nproc=$(nproc); load $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=1"
cd "$FH/ProjectFortress" && FORTRESS_THREADS=1 FORTRESS_JUNIT_VERBOSE=1 FORTRESS_CACHES="$S/caches" \
  java -Xmx768m -Xss32m -Djava.io.tmpdir="$S/tmp" -Dfortress.caches="$S/caches" -Dtests="$S/tests" \
       -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.tests.unit_tests.SystemJUTest 2>&1 | grep -v '^\s*at ' | sed "s#$FH/##g"
echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
rm -rf "$S"

\section{Restrictions on Coercion Declarations}
\seclabel{restrictions-coercion}
We place two restrictions on coercion declarations to ensure that it is
always possible to resolve coercions.

It is a static error for a type to define a coercion from any of its
subtypes.  For example, the following program is statically rejected:
%trait Number
%  coerce(z:ZZ) = ...
%end

%trait ZZ extends Number end
\begin{Fortress}
\(\KWD{trait} \TYP{Number}\)\\
{\tt~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(  \KWD{coerce}(z\COLONOP\mathbb{Z}) = \ldots\)\-\\\poptabs
\(\KWD{end}\)\\[4pt]
\(\KWD{trait} \mathbb{Z} \KWD{extends} \TYP{Number} \KWD{end}\)
\end{Fortress}
Instead, \VAR{z} of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} can be coerced to type
\TYP{Number} by
%coerce_[\Number\](z)
``\EXP{\mathrm{coerce}\llbracket\TYP{Number}\rrbracket(z)}''
where \EXP{\mathrm{coerce}} is defined in \library\
Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:87:declare instead, siblings under \TYP{Number}, with the coercions they declare:
Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:97:%%     extends { Number, IntegerLike[\ZZ\],
Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:198:{\tt~~~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(    \KWD{extends} \{\, \null\)\pushtabs\=\+\(\TYP{Number}, \TYP{IntegerLike}\llbracket\mathbb{Z}\rrbracket,\)\\
Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:305:The listing and the method entries below extend \TYP{Number} in place of
Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:32:They are siblings under the trait \TYP{Number}:
Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:100:%%     extends { Number, StandardPartialOrder[\QQ\], StandardMinMax[\QQ\],
Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:153:{\tt~~~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(    \KWD{extends} \{\, \null\)\pushtabs\=\+\(\TYP{Number}, \TYP{StandardPartialOrder}\llbracket\mathbb{Q}\rrbracket, \TYP{StandardMinMax}\llbracket\mathbb{Q}\rrbracket,\)\\

the results of dividing any integer by any nonzero integer,
and three more elements:
\EXP{+\infty} and \EXP{-\infty} (written \EXP{1/0} and \EXP{-1/0}),
the results of dividing a positive or a negative integer by zero,
and the indefinite rational (written \EXP{0/0}), which is used as the result
of dividing zero by zero or of adding \EXP{-\infty} to \EXP{+\infty}.

The number types of this chapter are
the integer types \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32},
\EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, and \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} (\secref{basic-integers}),
the rational type \EXP{\mathbb{Q}},
and the floating-point types \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} (\STR{RR64}) and \EXP{\mathbb{R}32} (\STR{RR32}).
They are siblings under the trait \TYP{Number}:
each is a subtype of \TYP{Number}, and none is a subtype of another.
Some conversions between them are coercions (\chapref{conversions-coercions}),
each declared by the type converted to;
since coercions do not chain (\secref{coercion}), each pair is declared.
Those among the integer types are given in \secref{basic-integers};
the others are these:

\begin{tabbing}
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}} (\STR{QQ}) coerces from \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, and \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}.
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{R}64} (\STR{RR64}) coerces from \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}, from \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and from integer numerals (\secref{literals}).
\end{tabbing}

Every other conversion between number types is written explicitly;
in particular, a conversion into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} from
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, or \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}
is explicit, written \EXP{\VAR{asFloat}(x)} with the method that \library\ declare on \TYP{Number}.

That is before row 552's edit (22:11) and its build (22:12-22:13).

- `88af50016` (21:56:41, `xUXZzJ`): `ComprisesUnlistedExtender.fss` and `.test` alone. They were seen failing at 21:56:16 on the key's commit, walk unchanged (`goSB4s`): `f(S)` / ` Missing expected refusal at load` / `Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1`.
- `c6aa596cd` (22:16:59): `GenericBesidePlainOverlapShapes.fss` alone, before the fix commit `4b2d97c75` (22:17:40). It was **written after row 552's edit was built** (build at 22:12:14-22:13:40, `Bf1DbQ`; test at 22:16:27, `wuMzjZ`). It was run in the rung's base copy (`FORTRESS_HOME=/home/user/fortress-walkload-base`, header `tree fa14a190c`): ` UNEXPECTED exception` / `with generic type, ...` / `Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1`.
- `0cf9834c1` (22:43:40): `ComprisesGenericChildUnlistedExtender` alone. It was **written after the closure check had been built four times** (22:20 to 22:40). Its failure was seen at 22:43:05 (`6VkM6k`) with the key's `FileTests` classes over the base's walk: ` Missing expected refusal at load` / `Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1`. Its first version, which declared `f(x: A)` beside `f(x: B)`, was refused on the base for that unrelated pair (22:42:27, `xdSLgW`) and was rewritten. The report does not say so.
- `524852baf` (22:47:08): the closure check. The last build of the code was at 22:44:43-22:46:18 (`nFMXYK`), with no edit after it. The 22-file run at 22:46:26 (`5ENrR1`) gave `OK (22 tests)`.
- The interpreter suite was run once, after the last code commit, on `code 524852baf` (tree `6e192f7f3`, `tmp/rung-walk-load-check/corpus-0.log` and `corpus-1.log`): `OK (246 tests)` and `OK (243 tests)`, each ending `EXIT=0`.

The build in the worktree (`BuildEnvironments.class` 22:46:09, `FileTests.class` 22:46:16) is the head's code. Every fix had a test that was seen failing before the fix was first built: `GenericBesidePlainTwoBounds` for row 552 and `ComprisesUnlistedExtender` for row 551. The two later tests were seen failing on the base's code before their fix commits, though after the fixes were built. That is a finding, not a ground to refuse.

## 2. The key against the compiled harness's keys

The key reads `Name.test` with `java.util.Properties`, keeps the `load_` keys and composes them with `ProjectProperties` (`FileTests.java:840-862`). It judges them with the compiled tests' own `generalTestFailed("load_", ...)` (`FileTests.java:490`). The compiled harness reads its keys with `StringMap.FromFileProps` and judges them with `generalTestFailed(command + "_", ...)` (`FileTests.java:702-703` at the base). The form is the same and the evaluator is the same.

The compiled harness and the key read an `XXX` name differently. A compiled `XXX` test with `compile_err_contains` passes when the compile fails with that text. A tests/ `XXX` file with a `load_` key passes only when the program loads and runs clean (`FileTests.java:494-496`). Under this reading:
- an `XXX` file asserts the refusal the specification asks for, and is an expected failure while walk loads the program, as home 2 asks;
- it goes red when walk refuses as named, or when the program fails in any other way. So the record's stop, "a key that lets an `XXX` file pass when the program fails for another reason than the refusal it names", is not met.

My own probes of the key, run with `harness-one.sh` on the rung's build (`tmp/rung-walk-load-check/skeptic/key/harness.log`, header `tree 6e192f7f3`):

    . interpret .../SkKeyTopInit       OK Saw expected refusal at load
    . interpret .../XXXSkKeyTopInit    Refused at load as its keys name       (red)
    . interpret .../SkKeyFrontEnd      Failed after load / Variable undefinedThing is not defined.   (red)
    . interpret .../SkKeyTypo          OK Saw expected refusal at load

- `SkKeyTopInit` is a plain test keyed `load_exception_contains=FailCalled`. It calls `fail` in a top-level variable's initializer. A run-time failure there counts as a refusal at load, because `Driver.evalComponent` initializes top-level variables (`cw.initVars()`, `Driver.java:244`) and `thrownAtLoad` looks for that frame (`FileTests.java:870-879`). The report's decision 3 says a run-time `FailCalled` whose text met the key was judged "Failed after load". That holds only for a failure in `run`.
- `SkKeyFrontEnd`: a refusal by walk's front end, before `evalComponent`, is reported as "Failed after load". The verdict is right and the words are wrong.
- `SkKeyTypo`: a misspelled key (`load_exception_contain`) is ignored, so the plain test passes on any refusal at load. Here the refusal was an unrelated overload pair. The compiled harness has the same weakness for its own keys.

None of these changes a verdict of a test the rung adds.

## 3. The closure check against the traits chapter and `everyKnownSubtypeListed`

The paragraph read in full: `Specification/basic/traits.tex`, section "Trait Declarations", the comprises paragraph and its revision callout. The checker read: `TypeHierarchyChecker.scala:257-287`.

The check implements the text's three forms:
- a subtype of a listed type;
- a trait whose own clause lists only such types (`closedAndCovered`);
- a generic trait that at least one trait or object extends, every immediate extender being below a listed type, with the static arguments substituted by position.

The last is as `everyKnownSubtypeListed` reads it, with one difference. It substitutes by position where the checker compares spellings (row 489), so it is more exact than the checker.

My programs (`tmp/rung-walk-load-check/skeptic/`): walk with `bin/fortress P.fss` at the head and in `/home/user/fortress-walkload-base`; the compiled path with `fortress compile` and `fortress run` in the base copy, since the rung changes nothing the compiled path reads and the worktree's `bytecode_cache` is empty after its `ant compileAll`.

| program | head (walk) | base (walk) | compiled |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SkUnlistedShape`: `object Tri extends Shape`, Shape lists Circle, Square | refused, "Invalid comprises clause: Shape has a comprises clause but its immediate subtype Tri is not eligible to extend it" | `other` | refused, same words |
| `SkGenericChildListed2`: AnyIntegral's shape (`N[\X extends N[\X\]\] extends AnyN`, listed objects `N8`, `N16`) and a listed object pair | `n8 n16 no` | `n8 n16 no` | `n8 n16 no` |
| `SkGenericChildDeep`: `M extends N[\M\]` unlisted, `N8 extends M` listed | refused, "...immediate subtype N ...; M extends it and is a subtype of none of the types the clause lists" | `loaded` | refused at N |
| `SkGenericObjectChild`: `object Odd[\T\]() extends Opt[\T\]` beside the listed `Sm[\T\]`, `Nn[\T\]` (the shape of the library's `Reflect`) | refused, "Opt ... Odd" | `loaded` | refused, same |
| `SkCrossUnlisted`: `S comprises { U, V }` in the program's own component `SkClosedLib`, `object Z extends S` in main | `f(S)` | `f(S)` | refused, "Invalid comprises clause: SkClosedLib.S has a comprises clause but its immediate subtype Z is not eligible to extend it" |
| `SkNonMain551`: row 551's own set, all in the program's own component `SkLib551`, called from main | `f(S)` | `f(S)` | `SkLib551.fss` refused, "S ... Z" and "T ... Z" (4 errors) |
| `SkObjExpr551`: row 551's set in main with `z = object extends { S, T } end` | `f(S)` | `f(S)` | checker passes; code generation "emitDesc of type AND(S,T) failed" |
| `SkGenericChildListed`: adds `Expr[\T\] comprises { IntE, BoolE }`, `IntE extends Expr[\ZZ32\]` | `n8 n16 no` | `n8 n16 no` | refused, "IntE is included in the comprises clause of Expr but IntE does not extend Expr[\T\]" |

The first five rows agree with the checker, and the repair is right for them.

The rows `SkCrossUnlisted`, `SkNonMain551` and `SkObjExpr551` are the fourth outcome of rule 4. The text settles each against walk, and the repair is outside what lands:
- the first two because the check reads only the main component's clauses (`BuildEnvironments.java:1186`);
- the third because object expressions are not read.

`SkNonMain551` is row 551's own program. Row 551's note reads "the closure is row 487's across components and this row's within one". "Within one" means one component, any component. So row 551 is not closed by this rung, and decision 6's sentence "Reading the main component's clauses repairs row 551, whose own scope is one component" is wrong.

`SkGenericChildListed` is the clause's other half, which the report lists as not checked. The text ("these statements hold of each instantiation") refuses it.

Neither the decision's reason nor the stop applies to a component of the user's own program. The withheld wider readings refuse the library's `Reflect` and the team tests, both of which are the library's clauses. A reading of every component outside the library would refuse `SkCrossUnlisted` and `SkNonMain551` and leave `Reflect` and the team tests alone. Decision 6 does not consider it, and it goes to Pavol.

## 4. The overlap reading against "Declarations with Static Parameters"

The section reads a declaration with static parameters as one declaration whose parameter type ranges over its instances. The Meet Rule there asks for declarations more specific than both that cover their common calls.

The edit reads each position of the generic as an over-approximation of the values it takes in any instance:
- a type parameter as its bounds that name no static parameter;
- a type that mentions a static parameter as `Any`;
- any other type as itself.

It also asks every cover to lie inside an instance of the generic (`instanceHolding`, `OverloadedFunction.java:868-870`) and below the plain domain. So it loads only sets whose real overlap is covered.

`intersectionPieces` with two types is `overlapPieces` itself (`OverloadedFunction.java:928`), and a plain pair is passed one type per position (`OverloadedFunction.java:822-824`). So no pair read before is read differently.

My programs, the same three ways:

| program | head | base | compiled |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SkSameParamTwice` (`pick[\T extends Aa\](x: T, y: T)`, `pick(Ao, Any)`, meet `pick(Ao, Aa)`) | `meet generic aoAny` | the same | the same |
| `SkSameParamTwiceUncovered` (meet only on `(Ao, Ao)`) | refused, "with generic type, ..." | refused | refused, "Invalid overloading of pick" |
| `SkBoundNamesOther` (`rel[\U extends Aa, T extends U\](x: T, y: U)`, a bound naming another static parameter) | `meet boAny` | refused, "with generic type, ..." | `meet boAny` |
| `SkNatInType` (`sized[\nat n\](x: Vec[\n\], y: ZZ32)`) | `meet v3Any` | `meet v3Any` | `meet v3Any` |

All agree with the checker. `SkBoundNamesOther` is a shape the worker's tests do not hold, a bound naming another parameter, and it is repaired.

The question of a loud failure becoming a quiet value: refusals at load ("with generic type, at least one pair of parameters must have excluding types") of sets the specification allows now load, and each call runs the most specific declaration (`SkBoundNamesOther` prints `meet boAny`, the compiled answer). The closure check goes the other way, making walk loud where it was quiet. The `catch (RuntimeException ex)` in `termOf` (`BuildEnvironments.java:1311-1316`, `:1322-1327`) turns a name walk cannot resolve into an unresolved term, and such a term can only fail to match. No valid program of mine or of the suite was refused.

## 5. The home-2 files against their rows and passages

Each passage was read in full: `overloading.tex` sections "Principles of Overloading", "Subtype Rule", "Meet Rule" with its paragraph "The Meet Rule for Functional Methods", and "Declarations with Static Parameters"; `traits.tex` section "Trait Declarations"; `exceptions.tex` section "Types of Exceptions".

Each comment line says what its section says. Each file has one comment line and no line citation. Each `.test` holds one `load_exception_contains` key.

The compiled path on copies of the five programs:
- row 534's: "A functional which takes a single parameter of a parametric type bound by Any cannot be overloaded."
- row 544's: "Invalid overloading of tag in trait V".
- row 549's: "There are multiple declarations of tie with the same parameter type: (Wide, Wide)".
- row 22's: compiles and runs, printing `Value`, rc=0. The compiled prelude's `Number` has no `comprises` clause (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:510`).
- row 487's: "Integral is undefined".

So the report's sentence on row 22's program and the team tests, "The text refuses each of them, and so does the checker", holds for the checker over the one library (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:360-361`), not for the compiled run.

The specification's prose does not close `Number`. `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex`, at "They are siblings under the trait Number", names the number types as siblings and gives no clause. The closure is the library's. `Exception`'s closure is the prose's: `exceptions.tex`, "Every exception is a subtype of either type CheckedException or UncheckedException".

`tests/extendNumber.fss:15` carries the team's comment "We ought to be able to extend the builtin type Number." This is against the clause the library has had since 2012 (`comprises { RR64 }` at `a874948ac`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:349-352`). Row 588's proposed repair, editing that team test, runs against its stated intent.

## 6. Library types and team tests at load

From the worker's suite run, not repeated:
- every library type and team test passes;
- `ReflectTest`, `ReflectiveNumberTypes`, `ReflectiveQuickCheckTest`, `extendNumber`, `extendException`, `atomicList` and `typeTests` are `OK`;
- only the two refusal tests give `OK Saw expected refusal at load`.

The 489 tests are the 479 `.fss` files of the base plus `concurrentPrinting.sh` (480, batch 8's gated sum) plus nine new `.fss` files. The demos are outside the suite. By reading, the demos whose own components declare closed traits (`BirdCount1m`-`r`, `Lambda`, `Words`, `aStar`, `IntegrationStats`, `turnersParaffins0`, `wordcount2`) list every extender of their clauses.

## 7. Other checks

- **Provenance block (check 2).** Every `file:line` was opened and says what the block says. The `historical:` line names all four files of the 2012 tree the diff edits.
- **Competing declarations (check 7).** None. No new component name exists elsewhere under `ProjectFortress/`, and the new Java names (`checkComprisesClauses`, `ComprisesCheck`, `intersectionPieces`, `loadRefusalKeys`, `thrownAtLoad`, `refusalVerdict`) occur only in the four edited files.
- **No count table (check 10).** `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/Driver.java` is outside the paths the rule allows without a table. The report's section 9 gives the reason. I checked it: outside `interpreter/`, `Driver` is called only from `Shell.eval` (`Shell.java:621`), the test command (`Shell.java:1221`) and `FileTests`. Neither stage can read the change.
- **Decisions on record (check 12).** The landed text agrees with "`AnyIntegral`'s closure and how the checker reads `comprises`" (`everyKnownSubtypeListed`, at least one extender) and with "The static-parameter sentence goes" (walk by declared domains). The batch record's intro lifts the stop "the clause and walk stay as they are" for this rung.
- **Threads.** The rung touches no mutable state. Walk ran at the default thread count and the harness at `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`.

## 8. Required corrections

1. Row 551 is not closed by this rung. The record says it is repaired for the main component's clauses only. The row stays open (or a new row is opened) for two cases, quoting `SkNonMain551` and `SkObjExpr551` (both print `f(S)` under walk at `6e192f7f3`):
   - a clause and its unlisted extender in another component of the program;
   - an object expression that extends a closed trait unlisted.

   Decision 6's sentence in the report ("Reading the main component's clauses repairs row 551, whose own scope is one component") is corrected to say this.
2. The report's section 5 sentence "The text refuses each of them, and so does the checker", and the matching divergence for row 22's program and the team tests, say that the compiled run of row 22's program prints `Value`. The compiled prelude's `Number` is open (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:510`), and the checker refuses the program only over the one library.
3. Decision 3 and section 3 of the report say that a failure while top-level variables are initialized counts as a refusal at load (`Driver.java:244`; `SkKeyTopInit`).
4. The report's step 7 says that the first version of `ComprisesGenericChildUnlistedExtender` was refused on the base for its unrelated `f(x: A)`, `f(x: B)` pair and was rewritten. Steps 5 and 7 say each test was written after its fix was built.
